facts.text: The user asked for an analogy to explain design tokens in simple terms.
The user said the first analogy was flawed because drawings can look very different even when using the same crayons.
The user said the analogy did not clearly describe why design tokens are superior to other approaches.
The user wanted the analogy revised to use a bakery comparison.
The user suggested symbolizing design tokens as recipes for frosting and batter.
The user said the same batter can be used for different styles of cakes.
The user said standardizing a component simplifies the decision when making many different cakes.
The user was confused about how changes propagate throughout a project.
The user asked whether changing a design system token would immediately update all live applications that use the design system.
The user asked whether users would immediately see the difference after a design system token change.
The user asked to revise the 3rd paragraph of the bakery example to make it clearer.
The user asked to avoid the word "propagate" in the revised paragraph.
The user asked to incorporate the bakery ingredient metaphor explicitly in the revised paragraph.
The user asked to clean up a revised paragraph without changing it significantly.
The user asked to give the whole thing again after cleaning up the paragraph.
The user provided text stating that design tokens simplify updating and maintaining consistency across applications.
The user provided an example where updating a frosting recipe makes cakes use sweeter frosting from that point on.
The user provided an example that updating a design token makes designs incorporate the change without being individually managed.
